test_title: RRB Technician Grade 1 19 Dec 2024 Shift 2 Official Paper
subject: general
question: In a survey of 350 students in a college, 150 students were found to be taking tea and 225 taking coffee, 100 were taking both tea and coffee. Find how many students were taking neither tea nor coffee?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Students taking either **Tea** or **Coffee** = (Tea + Coffee) − Both

⇒ (150 + 225) − 100 = 275

Students taking **neither** = Total Students − Students taking at least one drink

⇒ 350 − 275 = 75

**∴ The correct answer is 75 students.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total students n(U) = 350

Students taking **Tea** n(T) = 150

Students taking **Coffee** n(C) = 225

Students taking **both** n(T ∩ C) = 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d25905461315cc3e482e07337d1a28fc9407a1a835013ac1e010299fe4e82e2d.png] 

**Formula Used:**

n(T ∪ C) = n(T) + n(C) − n(T ∩ C)

Students taking **Neither** = n(U) − n(T ∪ C)

**Calculations:**

⇒ n(T ∪ C) = 150 + 225 − 100

⇒ n(T ∪ C) = 375 − 100 = 275

⇒ Students taking neither = 350 − 275

⇒ Students taking neither = 75

**∴ The correct answer is 75 students.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Venn Diagram Basics

The union of two sets A and B represents the total number of elements in either or both sets, calculated as n(A∪B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A∩B).

De Morgan's Laws

The number of elements in neither set is given by n(A' ∩ B'), which is equal to n(U) − n(A ∪ B).

Only One Set

Elements belonging to ONLY set A = n(A) − n(A ∩ B). In this question, students taking **only Tea** = 150 − 100 = 50.</p
